title: Trail and Escarpment
premise: Isandro Ishikawa, a desert ranger who has spent fifteen years erasing himself into the escarpment country, is hired by his old rival Sef Almada to recover a stolen ledger before the first snows seal the high passes. The thief turns out to be Isandro's presumed-dead sister Marisol, who took the ledger because it records the water rights their family sold to survive the drought that killed their parents. Crossing the range, the crew fractures as each member's claim on the ledger surfaces, and Isandro must choose between the inheritance of silence he built his life on and the truth Marisol carries. In the end he burns the ledger at the summit shrine, freeing both siblings from the past at the cost of the only proof of their family's name.
about_author: R. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former backcountry surveyor who spent a decade mapping arid ranges across the American Southwest before turning to fiction. Their work explores how landscapes keep the accounts people try to settle and fail to.

chapters.title: The Nothing That Tracks Back
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Tracking a horse thief through the basin, Isandro reflects on the wilderness's unforgiving arithmetic while recovering the stolen mare with quiet competence. The emotional beat is controlled solitude—until he finds a second set of tracks, deliberate and familiar, circling his own camp at night.

chapters.title: A Debt in Dry Country
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Sef Almada arrives with a contract: recover a ledger stolen from the Almada trading post before snow closes the passes, paying triple for discretion. Isandro refuses—the job touches the Ishikawa name—then finds the thief's trail leads toward the old family homestead. Beat: dread dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Crew of the Sworn-Off
chapters.summary: POV Tomas, the crew's young farrier. Assembling at the last waystation, the crew—Tomas, tracker Odile, and Sef himself—tests loyalties over bad coffee and worse history. Tomas idolizes Isandro but notices how Sef watches him like a man holding collateral. Beat: uneasy fellowship before the climb.

chapters.title: What the Homestead Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the ruined Ishikawa homestead, Isandro reads signs no one else can: the thief camped here, knew where things were buried. He uncovers his mother's grave marker disturbed and realizes the thief is family. Flashbacks surface the drought, the sale, the sister lost to it. Beat: grief breaking through professional calm.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. On the run above the tree line, Marisol reveals her side: she survived the drought years in exile and stole the ledger to prove the Almadas cheated her parents out of water rights. She knows Isandro is behind her and leaves messages only he would read. Beat: defiant hope shadowed by fear of being seen.

chapters.title: The Pass Narrows
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Snow flurries arrive early; the crew catches Marisol's fire ring still warm. Odile, who owes Sef a debt of her own, warns Isandro that Sef plans to bury the ledger's contents, not retrieve them. First blood: a rockslide, likely triggered, injures Tomas. Beat: trust beginning to fracture under altitude and suspicion.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro finally corners Marisol in a cave sheltering from a storm. Fifteen years of assumed death collide with accusation—he abandoned her name, she abandoned him—and Sef's crew closes in outside. They strike an uneasy truce: read the ledger together, then decide. Beat: raw sibling reckoning.

chapters.title: Sef's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Sef confronts them at the summit approach, revealing he bought the Ishikawa debt honestly but profited from the falsified sale ever since; returning the ledger ruins him. He offers Isandro his old life back—visibility, standing, absolution—for the book. Beat: temptation priced exactly right to wound.

chapters.title: Escarpment
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Climax at the summit shrine in the storm: Sef's hired gun turns on them, Tomas chooses Isandro over his paymaster, and Marisol nearly falls defending the ledger. Isandro saves Sef from the same ice that takes the gunman, refusing to let survival cost another life. Beat: violence resolving into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Ash on the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. At the shrine, brother and sister burn the ledger together—erasing the debt, the fraud, and the proof of their name in one act. Sef descends empty-handed and changed; the crew scatters with stories they won't tell. Isandro walks down into spring thaw no longer invisible, just known. Beat: costly peace.
